stem: During a science class in Meerut, Riya looks at a drop of pond water under the microscope and sees a single-celled Amoeba moving and feeding on its own. Her classmate Arjun says, “It has only one cell, so it cannot be a complete living organism.” Which statement is correct?

options.text: Arjun is correct, because every living organism must be made of many cells.
Riya is correct to disagree, because the single cell of an Amoeba carries out all life processes, so it is a complete organism.
Arjun is correct, because unicellular organisms can feed but cannot reproduce on their own.
Neither is correct, because an Amoeba becomes a complete organism only after joining with other cells.

teacher.key_rationale: An Amoeba is a unicellular organism whose single cell performs all survival functions (nutrition, respiration, reproduction), so it is a complete living organism; option B states this correctly.
